title: Celestial Tidal Bobbles
definition: The oscillations caused by the gravitational interaction between a celestial body and its host system, often resulting in a combination of vertical and horizontal movements.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of a cork on water. A tilted spinning object (like our solar system) wobbles and moves around as it orbits within a larger flat system (like the Milky Way), creating up-and-down bobbles and side-to-side wiggles.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Celestial tidal bobbles are the result of a tilted celestial body orbiting within a larger system. This interaction causes the celestial body to oscillate vertically and horizontally, creating a pattern of movement. In our case, the Sun's bobble within the Milky Way's gravitational field causes galactic tides.
difficulty_levels.expert: Celestial tidal bobbles are a manifestation of the complex three-body problem in orbital mechanics. They arise from the gravitational interaction between a celestial body and its host system, with the celestial body's orbital plane being tilted relative to the host system's plane. This creates a combination of vertical and horizontal movements, with the vertical movement occurring when the celestial body crosses the host system's equatorial plane, and the horizontal movement resulting from the uneven gravitational pull from the host system's spiral arms. This phenomenon has been observed in numerous celestial systems, including our solar system within the Milky Way.

extra_fields.insight: The combination of the Sun's 60° tilt relative to the Milky Way and its orbital motion creates celestial tidal bobbles that have been measured and observed by scientists.
